newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rises to 10.661 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rises to 10.661 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate rose to an average of 10.661 percent at the regular weekly auction from the previous 10.653 percent, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
The other maturities also rose. The 182-day bill rate edged up to an average of 11.073 percent from 11.067; and the 364-day bill rate jumped to 11.532 from 11.504 percent.
The government awarded 4.5 billion pesos out of the 17.185 billion pesos worth of tenders received at the auction.
"The market is just moving sideways," a foreign bank dealer said, adding that the latest rates were just slightly higher from their previous levels.
He said interest rates were expected to hover at current levels since the Central Bank had not changed its interest rates despite the high liquidity in the market.

The most preferred maturity was the 182-day bill with tenders worth 8.230 billion pesos because its rate was almost at par with the 364-day bill, dealers said. A total of 1.5 billion pesos were accepted for the 182-day bills.
The 364-day bills, with sales of 2.0 billion pesos, had bids worth 5.130 billion pesos.
The three-month bills generated tenders worth 3.825 billion pesos, of which 1.0 billion pesos were awarded.
